security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU, mseccfg CSR access guard (have_mseccfg) and migration subsection guard (mseccfg_needed) use diverging extension checks: have_mseccfg checks ext_smepmp, ext_zkr, ext_smmpm but omits ext_zicfilp, while mseccfg_needed includes ext_zicfilp. When a VM is configured with only Zicfilp (no Smepmp/Zkr/Smmpm), the CSR traps as illegal but its state is still included in the migration stream, creating a guest-observable inconsistency where migrated-in mseccfg state exists but cannot be accessed or modified.
security_spec.summary: have_mseccfg() CSR access guard missing ext_zicfilp check causes divergence from mseccfg_needed() migration guard; mseccfg state is migrated but guest cannot access it, violating spec rule that mseccfg exists when any field-defining extension (including Zicfilp) is implemented

findings.finding: have_mseccfg() omits ext_zicfilp in its extension check, while mseccfg_needed() (machine.c:430-431) includes it. When a VM is configured with only Zicfilp (no Smepmp/Zkr/Smmpm), CSR_MSECCFG traps as illegal-instruction, making the MLPE bit (bit 10 of mseccfg) inaccessible to the guest. However, the mseccfg state is still included in the migration stream via mseccfg_needed(), creating a guest-observable inconsistency: migrated-in mseccfg state exists (and MLPE controls M-mode forward-edge CFI per the priv-cfi spec) but cannot be read or written by the guest. Additionally, cpu.c:762-764 only clears mseccfg on reset when ext_smepmp is set, so with only Zicfilp, env->mseccfg is not reset either. The fix is to add ext_zicfilp to the have_mseccfg() checks and to the reset condition.

spec_citations.excerpt:
|===
|Privilege Mode| xLPE
|  M           | csr:mseccfg[mlpe]
|  S or HS     | csr:menvcfg[lpe]
|  VS          | csr:henvcfg[lpe]
|  U or VU     | csr:senvcfg[lpe]
|===

findings.finding: Reset code only clears env->mseccfg when ext_smepmp is set. When only ext_zicfilp is enabled, env->mseccfg is not explicitly reset. While env is zero-initialized on creation, this means mseccfg is not cleared on warm reset when only Zicfilp is configured. After fixing have_mseccfg, this reset condition should also include ext_zicfilp (and ext_zkr, ext_smmpm) for correctness.

mseccfg_needed() correctly checks all four extensions (ext_smepmp, ext_zkr, ext_smmpm, ext_zicfilp) that use the mseccfg CSR. This is the correct superset — migration should include the state whenever any of these extensions is present.
